findings.comment:
Observed the following areas that are in need of cleaning or a change of container to prevent cross-contamination of food:

The baffles are a portion of the hood system able to be cleaned by the facility staff. See that the baffles are cleaned at a frequency suitable to maintain them clean and free of hanging debris. 
(ii) Observed a grocery sack being used to store dried orange peel that will be used for a future sauce. Grocery sacks are not an approved food-grade package. CORRECTED: Staff moved the orange peels to a food-grade package.
(iii) Observed trays of food in the 2-door freezer without a cover. Foods that are not actively cooling should be covered.
(iv) Observed uncovered marinating chicken in a bulk container within the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED: covered with baking sheets during the inspection.
(v) Observed the shelving in the walk-in cooler the have some mold growth along the right side beneath the fans. Also, observed a molded can being used to support the base shelving of the lowest right base shelf beneath the fans. See that the shelving is cleaned and the molded can is removed from use. 
(vi) Observed grocery sacks being used to store foods in the reach-in freezers in the back room. See above - cease use of grocery bags for food storage. 
Ensure that food items are covered to prevent cross-contamination or that equipment is cleaned to prevent contamination of food.

findings.comment:
Observed that staff who are handling food do not have Food Handler certificates. Discussed with PIC that there are courses available online in Chinese. Ensure that all staff who are handling food are Food Handler certification from an accredited program.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.citation_text:

The steamer was turned-off overnight and the food was temped at 50F today. Owner stated that he was going to discard the product, however, the facility should remove old food at the end of the night. findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature
findings.comment: Inspector observed cooling lo mien noodles in a medium sized metal bowl stored on the back shelves of the walk-in cooler. The noodles were approximately 78 degrees based on a digital probe-style thermometer reading. No logs are kept to record cooling times and temperatures to verify the two-hour mark had not been surpassed. Per 3-501.14 of the 2017 FDA Food Code, foods must be removed from heat and cooled quickly to prevent the growth of dangerous pathogens known to cause foodborne illness in cooling TCS foods. Foods must cool from an initial temperature of 135 degrees F after cooking to a temperature of 70 degrees F within 2 hours. Foods must cool from 135 degrees F after cooking to a temperature of 41 degrees F within 6 hours. Ensure that the facility adheres to these time/temperature requirements when cooling foods within the facility. Inspector will re-evaluate on 04/14/2023.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Underneath the food storage shelving across from the entry to the walk-in cooler, there is an area of vinyl coving which has peeled away from the wall. This trim must be repaired/replaced to ensure a smooth, non-absorbent and easily cleanable surface where food storage is occurring.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
The hood has begun to accumulate oil residue and debris which has the potential to contaminate food being cooked on the stove underneath. Operator to contact the hood cleaning service to clean the hood. Ensure that the hood is cleaned regularly and at a frequency which precludes the accumulation of oil residue and other debris.

findings.comment:

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
Inspector observed several in-use utensils including multiple whisks stored on top of the smoker. The smoker top is not a cleaned and sanitized surface. (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:

These areas continue to be harborage conditions however as there is a significant amount of debris and residue behind the prep cooler and freezer. If you see any live roaches while cleaning these areas, contact Orkin to have another treatment completed. 

Inspector will follow-up on 11/02/2022 during previously scheduled inspection for cleaning and removal of the dead roaches and to ensure no live roaches have returned at this time. 

6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Upon arrival to the facility, inspector notes minimal to no improvement on maintenance items from previous inspection. The following items must still be corrected:

- Cover the base of the walls behind the back dry storage area (locked area) which are peeling and deteriorating with trim to make them smooth and paint/wallpaper the bare drywall as those areas are used for storage of frozen items and sauces, both of which have the potential to spill. Bare drywall cannot be cleaned easily. Any surfaces throughout the facility that are subject to food or moisture but be SMOOTH, NON-ABSORBENT and EASILY CLEANABLE. Take time to go through the facility and identify areas of concern where surfaces are in need of repair/replacement to guarantee they can be cleaned easily. 

- The wall underneath the dry storage area of the main kitchen has trim which needs to be replaced or reattached to the wall. Go through the facility and identify areas with damaged and/or missing trim and reattach the trim to the wall. If trim cannot be reattached, replace it. These areas are prone to moisture and pest damage and allow entrance for pests. 

- Ceiling tiles throughout the facility including above the hand sink and in the back room need to be replaced. Go through and replace all ceiling tile which are damaged, missing, and/or molding. These open tile are not cleanable and allow pests to enter and live in the facility. They also present a food hazard by allowing materials from the ceiling above to contaminate food below. 

- Apply a bead of caulk to the triple basin sink in the kitchen. This is a high moisture area and water that flows behind the sink is not easily cleaned. Make sure that areas where water or other residue can drip down behind them are caulked or otherwise protected from spills. 

6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 
6-201.16: (A) Wall and ceiling covering materials shall be attached so that they are EASILY CLEANABLE. (B) Except in areas used only for dry storage, concrete, porous blocks, or bricks used for indoor wall construction shall be finished and SEALED to provide a SMOOTH, nonabsorbent, EASILY CLEANABLE surface.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Observed food preparation occurring without prior hand washing by employees. Ensure that employees are washing their hands regularly during food preparation and any time hands may become contaminated. 

2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed

2-301.15: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands in a HANDWASHING SINK only.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Hand washing sink was blocked by rubber dish washing gloves and scrubbing pads on arrival to the facility. Items were removed from the dry hand sink by operator. Ensure that the hand washing sink remains accessible at ALL times. 

5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Hand washing sink was not stocked with paper towels. Ensure that hand washing sinks are always stocked with paper towels and soap. 

6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.comment:
A can of tomato ketchup and a can of soy sauce were observed to have dents around the upper seal of the can potentially compromising the integrity of the seal. The cans are to be disposed of immediately. 

3-202.15: FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.comment:
Back room storage was observed to have open containers of rice, sugar and flour which were directly under broken and missing ceiling tiles, cleaning and pest control chemicals, a dirty wok, x2 fly strips with flies present, and other refuse. 

3-101.11: FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, honestly presented.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11:  The facility is observed to have uncovered foods throughout. There are opened cans of oyster and soy sauce in the kitchen and in the walk-in cooler. Boxes of chicken and 5 gallon buckets of sauce are observed uncovered in the walk-in cooler. At least five containers of fried chicken (General Tso) and one container of eggrolls uncovered in the kitchen and the back storage room. A colander of noodles was observed uncovered, without temperature control and in contact with the soiled bottom of the triple sink (discarded during the inspection). Also, observed a colander of rice noodles resting atop dirty dishes in the triple sink. The facility lacks the knowledge of proper safe food storage. The back storage room is observed to have fly strips soiled with flies, opened containers of rat poison next to opened bags of food, and chemicals in direct proximity to opened bags of food. The lack of cleaning combined with opened food items lends to possible cross-contamination. 
(A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-304.15: Hand washing was non-existent, but old, dirty gloves were observed throughout the facility. Used gloves were observed within the hand sink basin, on dry storage shelving, around the preparation cooler, over the fried chicken on the counters. One employee was observed attempting to pick-up a previously worn glove and inspector stopped the behavior. Revisit proper glove use with staff. Gloves need only be used with handling ready-to-eat items. Most of the foods are handled with a utensils. SCDPH is unclear why all the used gloves are observed throughout the facility. Staff will be need to demonstrate knowledge of proper glove use prior to reopening. 

(A) If used, SINGLE-USE gloves shall be used for only one task such as working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD or with raw animal FOOD, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-304.11: All food contact surfaces are observed soiled with a thick accumulation of soil. A soiled peeler was observed being used during the inspection. Activity was halted, peeler was sent to dish, and food was discarded. 
(A) FOOD shall only contact surfaces of EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS that are cleaned. (B) SINGLE-SERVICE/USE ARTICLES (C) LINENS

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-602.11: A tumbler for raw chicken is observed soiled from the morning use. Staff kept indicating the utensils were just used, however, dishes were piled within the triple sink, around the triple sink, and most equipment is observed soiled with days worth of soil. The smoker is observed with a thick accumulation of grease at the bottom and sides. The unit has not been cleaned of animal fats after possibly multiple days use. One cutting board is observed being stored in the mop sink. Another cutting board is observed on the floor resting against the garbage can and the walk-in cooler door. The final cutting board was observed coated in mold and old food and on top of the dry storage shelving. This cutting board was discarded, the other cutting boards were pulled to dish for cleaning. 
(D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-602.12: The outside of the woks is observed coated with accumulated char and grease from multiple use without cleaning. Preparation cooler has black mold and accumulated soil and grease around the back of the hinged-lid. 
(A) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking and baking EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at least every 24 hours. This section does not apply to hot oil cooking and filtering EQUIPMENT if it is cleaned as specified in Subparagraph 4-602.11(D)(6). (B) The cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least every 24 hours by using the manufacturer's recommended cleaning procedure.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:

The bowl is observed soiled with a multitude of foods: white powders, oils, soy sauce, crystallized white powders. Both items were pulled from use for cleaning. 
 (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature
findings.comment:
3-501.14: The facility had at least five containers of fried chicken throughout the kitchen and back storage room. One container of egg rolls is observed. Several food items were being brought to the walk-in cooler as inspectors were walking into the kitchen. The containers of chicken were probed at 80-110F/eggrolls were 90F. PIC stated that foods were made within the last thirty minutes. The food containers appeared cool to the touch and center of containers were the probed items. Containers are at least six inches in depth - too deep for appropriate cold holding. Cooling was discussed and emphasized the use of shallow pans or baking sheets combined with the speed rack in the walk-in cooler to allow for proper cooling. Will check on procedures and staff education. 
(A) TCS FOOD shall be cooled within in 2 hours from 135F to 70F. Within 6 hours, FOOD shall cool from 135F to 41F or less. (B) TCS FOOD shall be cooled within 4 hours or less if prepared from ingredients at ambient temperature. (C) TCS FOOD received above 45F in compliance with LAWS shall be cooled within 4 hours. (D) Raw EGGS shall be received and immediately placed in EQUIPMENT with air temperature of 45F or less.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.17: There are no dates on foods. Prepared foods in the walk-in cooler and preparation cooler are not date marked. 
(A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
findings.comment:
3-501.19:  Facility has had previous knowledge of the four hour rule and the need to label in-use foods held on the counter. There was observed foods throughout the facility and no time as control available. Chopped cabbage is observed in a tub by the preparation cooler without a time indicated. Discussed using a dry erase board, Post-It, of other method for controlling the time foods are pulled from cold holding and placed without temperature control. 
(A) If time without temperature used for public health control, written procedure approved by regulatory authority shall be available upon request (Pf). (B) If time is used as control for up to 4 hours, food shall have initial temperature of 41F (or less) or 135F (or greater). FOOD shall be marked, cooked and served within 4 hour time limit. If FOOD is unmarked or marked exceeding 4-hour limit, FOOD shall be discarded. (P) (C) If time is used as control for up to 6 hours, food shall have initial temperature of 41F or less. FOOD shall not exceed 70F. If FOOD is unmarked or marked exceeding 6-hour limit, FOOD shall be discarded. (D) HSP FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS cannot use time control for raw eggs.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
7-201.11: Observed rat poison, full fly strips, and spray bottles of chemicals stored in the back room in direct contact with bagged food powders. Discard open containers of food and properly organize the back room. 
 (A)-(B) POISONOUS MATERIALS shall be stored to prevent contamination of FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES by separating or locating MATERIALS in area away or below FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES (use partition or store below).

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
3-501.15:  The pans of cooling foods are too deep to allow for proper cooling. Methods used include keeping foods on counter until they are cool to touch, covering, and then moving to walk-in cooler. These are not appropriate strategies for cooling. Discussed shallow pans (2-3”) using a stem thermometer to monitor temperature (135-70F within two hours and 70-41F within four hours).  And not covering until cooled to 41F. 

(A) Cooling shall be accomplished with time and temperature criteria by using following methods: FOOD in shallow pans, Separating FOOD into small portions, using rapid cooling EQUIPMENT, stirring food in container placed in ice bath, containers facilitating heat transfer, adding ice, other effective methods. P (B) When placed in cooling or cold holding EQUIPMENT, FOOD containers shall be: arranged to maximize heat transfer through container walls, loosely covered or uncovered, and during cooling period. C

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment:
3-501.13: There is observed a box of shrimp ‘thawing’ under the triple sink - stored on the floor. The box is holding shrimp still under 41F and was moved to the walk-in cooler. 

TCS FOOD shall be thawed: (A) at 41F or below in refrigeration (B) completely submerged under running water, not getting above 41F (water temp of 70F or below). If food will be cooked, not getting above 41F for more than 4 hours. (C) part of the cooking process (D) Using any procedure if RTE FOOD is thawed and prepared for immediate service (E) ROP FISH that bear label shall be removed from packaging before thawing under refrigeration, upon completion of thawing from running water.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
4-302.12: The facility could not produce a probe-style thermometer. See that clean and readily available stem thermometers are present. 
(A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
4-204.112: Walk-in cooler and preparation coolers are not observed with thermometers. See that all cold holding devices have conspicuously placed cold holding units. 
 (A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature. (B) EQUIPMENT holding TCS FOOD shall have TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE affixed to device. (C) Does not apply to EQUIPMENT without practical means of measuring ambient air surroundings. (D) TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be designed to be easily readable. C (E) FOOD and water TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall have numerical scale, printed record, or digital readout in increments no greater than 1C or 2F in the intended range of use. Pf

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container
findings.comment:
3-302.12: Observed several containers of food to not have a recognizable materials. Several brown liquid containers were discarded. White powders are observed without labeling in the preparation cooler/kitchen area. Labels should be available on foods. 
 If in working container, FOOD not readily recognized or easily mistakable shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-501.115: Active juvenile roaches are observed running from beneath the reach-in freezer to the chicken tumbler. See that pest control is contacted to treat area - pests are likely within the reach-in freezer. 
(A) Live animals may not be allowed on PREMISES of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT (B) Live animals may be allowed on PREMISE under certain conditions if contamination of FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES does not occur. (C) Live or dead FISH bait may be stored if contamination of FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES is prevented.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
3-305.11: Observed bulk bag of cabbages stored on the soiled floor of the back room. Clean the floor and move the cabbages. Overall, there is a lack of understanding on how food should be properly protected from chemical and physical contamination. Educate staff on safe food storage and handling. See that the dry storage areas are used and food is stored on shelving at least 6” off the floor. 
(A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor. (B) FOOD in working containers and packages may be stored less than 6 inches on case lot handling EQUIPMENT. (C) Pressurized BEVERAGE containers, cased FOOD in waterproof containers, and milk containers in plastic crates may be stored on floor.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: There are observed wet and soiled wiping cloths on counters throughout the kitchen. Cloths are nearly black from repeated use without proper laundering. A sani-bucket is available and not being used. Store cloths in sani-buckets between uses. Discard cloths as they become black.  
(A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-802.11: There are observed blue cloths nearly blackened from use without laundering on counters of the facility. See that used cloths are laundered daily or discarded after being too soiled to make clean. Discard or clean in-use wiping cloths that are soiled. 
(A) LINENS not in direct contact with FOOD shall be laundered between operations if soiled. (B) Cloth gloves shall be laundered before being used with different raw animal FOOD. (C) LINENS and cloth napkins shall be laundered between customers, when being used as food holding liner. (D) Wet wiping cloths shall be laundered daily. (E) Dry wiping cloths shall be laundered as necessary to prevent contamination of FOOD and UTENSILS.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-903.11: Observed soiled-but-supposed-to-be-cleaned knives, whisks, spatulas, peelers stored in soiled, old cans and atop smoker. The cans were discarded during the inspection and some older utensils were also discarded. The facility still had soiled knives stored on dry storage shelving. See that all utensils are cleaned and stored in clean containers. 
(A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. (B) clean EQUIPMENT shall be stored in self-draining position that allows air drying, covered or inverted. (D) Items that are kept in closed PACKAGES may be stored below 6 inches if on dollies, pallets, racks, and skids properly designed.

findings.title: Gloves used properly
findings.comment:
3-304.15: Hands were never observed being washed and gloves were never observed being properly donned. Gloves were observed soiled and positioned throughout the kitchen in a manner that would allow for easy donning. Staff attempted to don gloves but was asked to stop. Possibly a dozen used, single gloves were discarded during the inspection. See that staff is educated on proper glove-use. 
 (B) Slash-resistant gloves used to protect hands shall be used with FOOD that is subsequently cooked. (C) Slash-resistant gloves may be used with RTE FOOD if gloves are SMOOTH, durable, and nonabsorbent, or if gloves are covered with SMOOTH, durable, nonabsorbent gloves. (D) Cloth gloves may not be used with direct contact with FOOD unless FOOD is cooked.

findings.citation_text: 750.540 (C) The food establishment is not under the operational supervision of a Certified Food Service Sanitation Manager that is present at appropriate times. Provide an adequate number of staff with approved training. Reference 750.540.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment: No conditional agreement forms have been signed nor knowledge of exlcusion or restriction can be provided. Ensure proper knowledge is provided to employees of facility. Sign conditional agreement form.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.11(C)(17) (Pf) PIC did not demonstrate knowledge of responsibilities for preventing the transmission of foodborne disease and exclusion or restriction of Food Employees. Discussed related section of the food code.  Reference 2-102.11(C)(17).

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment: Observed no vomit/diarrhea procedure present in facility. Handout provided. Corrected.
findings.citation_text: 2-501.11  (Pf) Establishment does not have procedures for employees to follow when responding to discharging of vomitus or fecal matter. Provide procedures to comply with this section of the code. Reference 2-501.11.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment: Observed food prep material and plastic from box inside of handsink. Ensure handsink is always accessible. Handwashing stations must be for handwashing only.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11  (Pf) Hand washing sink blocked by food prep material . Hand washing sinks must be accessible at all times. Reference 5-205.11.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment: Observed personal item (designated as meat) to be stored above cut onion. Ensure raw vegetables are stored above personal items as well as raw meats to prevent contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11  (P) cut onion stored below personal use meat . Store raw vegetables above personal items and raw meats to protect from cross-contamination. Reference 3-302.11.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment: Observed several foods to be exposed while in cold holding units. Ensure all food is covered when not in use. Cover food.
findings.citation_text: 3-307.11  (C) Food is not protected from contamination in cold holding units. Food shall be protected from contamination. Reference 3-307.11.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment: Observed handle of utensil to be touching dry food product. Ensure handle is extended outward and away from food.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.12  (C) In-Use Utensils are stored incorrectly in flour bags . Store in-use utensils: 1) in the food with the handle above the top of the food item; 2) on a clean and sanitized surface; 3) in running water; 4) in a container of hot water maintained at or above 135 ?F. Reference 3-304.12.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment: Observed sanitation bucket to be without sanitizer. Ensure sanitizer is present during times of operaiton. Corrected. Cl- 200ppm
findings.citation_text: 4-303.11 (B) Chemical sanitizers must be present during all times of operation. Reference 4-303.11.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: Observed grease build-up on hood vent. Observed soil accumulation on bottom of freezer. Clean non-food contact surfaces as needed to prevent accumulation and potential cross contamination.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(B) and (C)  (C)  Grease and soil accumulation present on hood vent and bottom of reach-in freezer. Thoroughly clean all cooking equipment and pans. Reference 4-601.11(B) and (C).

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment: Observed grease and boxes scattered near stove of kitchen area. Ensure floors are kept uncluttered and cleaned.
findings.citation_text: 6-201.11  (C) [Floors, Walls and Ceilings] in the kitchen area were found in a state of disrepair, or not to be smooth and easily cleanable. Except as specified in Section 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are smooth and easily cleanable.  Reference 6-201.11.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
Observed unlabeled unknown bulk product outside original container. Ensure proper labeling on all food products
750-130f Unless its identity is unmistakable, bulk food such as cooking oil, syrup, salt, sugar or flour not stored in the product container or package in which it was obtained, shall be stored in a container identifying the food by common name.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Observed several prepared foods in the walk-in fridge to be without date marks. Foods included, but not limited to, cooked chicken and shrimp. Person-in-Charge (PIC) was educated on topic and a follow-up will occur next week. All Time and temperature control for safety (TCS) foods must be held no longer than 7 days.
750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.comment:
Observed cabbage to be pressed with weight to excrete water content. Lettuce is out of temperature for unknown time. Proper storage of 41F or below for cut leafy greens must be practiced. 
750-153(a) Food shall not be held more that 4 hours past the point it is removed from temperature control. Do not hold food in excess of four hours after removal from temperature control.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
1) Observed open drinks to be present in food prep area. Open drinks are not allowed in kitchen. If drink is necessary, a straw and lid must be used and kept away from food prep area.
2) Ventilation has significant grease build-up. Ventilation must be cleaned as needed to prevent contamination. 
750-160  Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
Observed several foods to be uncovered in walk-in cooler. Food must be covered during long term storage and between uses.
750-120(a) Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
Observed tong handles to be in food. All in-use utensils must be stored with handle up to prevent contamination.
750-280 Food dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with the handle extending out of the food; or stored clean and dry; or stored in running potable water dipper wells.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment:
Observed employee switch tasks by placing gloves on hands without washing in between tasks. Employees must practice proper handwashing to prevent food contamination. This includes the proper technique and proper timing to do so when hands become soiled.
750-510a Employees shall properly wash their hands any time their hands may have become contaminated and prior to handling food or clean equipment.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Observed plastic containers to be used for cold holding. These containers laid on top of food. Ensure proper equipment is used for food. 
750-630 Safe plastic or safe rubber or safe rubber-like materials that, under the conditions of normal use, are resistant to scratching, scoring, decomposition, crazing, shipping, and distortion, that are of sufficient weight and thickness to permit cleaning and sanitizing by normal dishwashing methods and which meet the general requirements are permitted for repeated use.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
Observed microwave, grill rack, and can opener to be soiled with debris. Food-contact surfaces must be cleaned routinely to ensure equipment is free of grease, debris, and other accumulated soil. 
750-800d Food-contact surfaces of grills, griddles, and similar cooking devices and the cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least once a day.   The food-contact surfaces of all cooking equipment shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other accumulated soil.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed beverage holding cooler to be soiled on bottom rack as well as the oven. Non-food contact surfaces of equipment must be cleaned as needed to prevent debris build up. 
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment:
Observed no paper towels in women's restroom. All restrooms must have proper items to allow proper hand washing. 
750-1120 All restrooms must have self-closing doors, properly operating fixtures, be clean and have proper hand washing supplies in order to help facilitate good hygienic practices.  Provide properly designed and maintained restrooms.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Observed cardboard boxes, grease build-up, water, and food debris on the floor of the kitchen. Floors must be kept clean.
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.comment:
Observed some pork product still in the cooker unit-left overnight. Thrown away--Corrected--Discussed with owner that it must be cooled down in a walkin cooler or freezer and not left in unit overnight.
750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage (41°F or below, or 135°F or above)
750-150(b)  Hot potentially hazardous foods shall be maintained at 135°F or above except during the cooling process. Store hot foods at 135°F or above. (Except for rare roast beef which may be held at 130F.)

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
Observed bags of cabbage stored on the floor in the back room. Store cabbage up off the floor at least 6 inches. (CORRECTED)
750-130(b) Food shall be stored at least 6 inches off the floor.  Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: Foods handled with minimal manual contact
findings.comment:
Observed a clear container stored in the bbq sauce in white bucket floating. Provide a handled scoop or large spoon for sauce.
750-290 Ice shall be dispensed only with scoops, tongs, or other ice dispensing utensils.  Provide appropriate utensils for dispensing food (must have handle, no bowls used)

findings.title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)
findings.comment:
Observed a drink in a can on the prep table top of the 2 dr unit at wok. (CORRECTED) Drink was thrown away. Drinks are allowed in the back room away from food product and cooking surfaces.
750-530a Employees shall consume food only in designated dining areas. An employee dining area shall not be so designated if consuming food there may result in contamination of other food, equipment, utensils, or other items needing protection.

findings.title: Pre-flushed, scraped, soaked
findings.comment:
Observed dishes left from yesterday in the 3 compartment sink and on drain board. Bus tubs with food left in them. Wash all dishes before leaving for the night. 
750-820c Equipment and utensils shall be pre-flushed or pre-scraped and, when necessary, pre-soaked to remove gross food particles and soil.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment:
Observed dirty cold sanitizer water when I arrived under the wok. Bucket was dumped and cleaned and set up. 100ppm test. (CORRECTED)  This is a repeat violation--I am doing a re-inspection in 7 days to check the violation.
750-800b To prevent cross-contamination, kitchenware and food-contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed and sanitized after each use and following any interruption of operations during which time contamination may have occurred.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Repeat violation: the large fan in the kitchen with dust buildup. 2)upright freezer with ice accumulation. Clean the surfaces listed above.

Observed the smoker unit to have debris buildup, the top of the wok area with much splash from top to bottom. Clean the surfaces.


.

750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Hand washing sinks installed, located, accessible
findings.comment:
Observed many large containers stored in front of the chest freezer and the employee handwashing sink. (CORRECTED) Handwashing sink must always be available. Store dirty containers elsewhere.
750-1120(b) Lavatories shall be accessible to employees at all times.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment:
Observed the self closures on the restroom doors to be unattached to door. Attach the self closures.
750-1120 All restrooms must have self-closing doors, properly operating fixtures, be clean and have proper hand washing supplies in order to help facilitate good hygienic practices.  Provide properly designed and maintained restrooms.
Absence of toilet paper in the women's restroom. provide toilet paper for the women's restroom.
750-1110d Toilet facilities shall be kept clean and in good repair and free of objectionable odors. A supply of toilet tissue shall be provided at each toilet at all times. Easily cleanable, covered receptacles shall be provided for waste materials.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Repeat violation: The floor in the back kitchen area and under the wok with much food splash. Clean the floor in the kitchen area.
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
The ceiling vent in the dining area with much dust accumulation in the vent at the ceiling fan. Clean the vent and change filter.
750-1220 Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean. Clean the walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Premises maintained fee of litter, unnecessary articles. Cleaning and maintaining equipment properly...
findings.comment:
Mop head stored down in the mop sink. Store the head so it can facilitate air for drying.
750-1390 Maintenance and cleaning tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners and similar equipment shall be maintained and stored in a way that does not contaminate food.
